technique.how: Ask packs per day and years smoked; pack-years = packs/day x years (20 cigarettes = 1 pack). Record current vs former smoking and quit date, and ask about pipes, cigars, and other inhaled exposures.
technique.prerequisites: Reliable history from patient or collateral source.

interpretation.positive_finding: More than 40 pack-years substantially raises the probability of obstructive airway disease (LR 8.3 in CARE-COAD1) and makes COPD exacerbation a more plausible cause of dyspnea.
interpretation.negative_finding: A light or absent smoking history lowers but does not exclude obstructive airway disease; the RCE did not report an LR for the absence of heavy smoking.
interpretation.pitfalls: Pack-year recall is imprecise and biomass, occupational, and asthma-related airflow limitation occur in never-smokers. Smoking is also a risk factor for ACS and lung cancer, so it does not discriminate among smoking-related diagnoses.
interpretation.changes_what: Heavy pack-year history plus wheeze or known OAD shifts dyspnea toward COPD exacerbation; confirm with spirometry when stable.

estimates.target_condition: Obstructive airway disease (FEV1 and FEV1/FVC below 5th percentile) — finding PRESENT = smoking >40 pack-years
estimates.population: 309 consecutive patients at 25 primary care and referral sites in 14 countries (25% known OAD, 37% suspected, 39% neither); mean age 56
estimates.reference_standard: Spirometry: FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratio below the 5th percentile adjusted for height, age and sex

sources.citation: Straus SE, McAlister FA, Sackett DL, Deeks JJ. The accuracy of patient history, wheezing, and laryngeal measurements in diagnosing obstructive airway disease. CARE-COAD1 Group. JAMA. 2000.
Holleman DR, Simel DL. Does the clinical examination predict airflow limitation? JAMA. 1995.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not let a heavy smoking history anchor the dyspnea diagnosis on COPD when hypoxia, fever, chest pain or new edema suggest pneumonia, ACS, PE or heart failure.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Smokers with acute dyspnea and chest pain need ECG and troponin; smoking history does not lower ACS probability.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Self-reported pack-years; no reliability statistic reported in the abstract.

extraction_notes: Only an LR+ without CI is available from the abstract of CARE-COAD1 (multivariate model); no sensitivity/specificity, so partially_quantified. Prevalence 0.52 is from the same abstract ('52% had an FEV1 and FEV1-FVC ratio less than the fifth percentile'). The >=70 pack-year threshold in the title is attributed to Holleman & Simel 1995 (PMID 7815660, RCE 'Does the clinical examination predict airflow limitation?'); that record has no PubMed abstract and no open-access text, so no number is entered for it (LR ~8 for >=70 pack-years is unverified recall). Full JAMA text of Straus 2000 not open access; the multivariate table could not be inspected.
